What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(-6,0)$ and passes through the point $(-2,6).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-6,0),$ we substitute $h=-6$ and $k=0$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+6).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-2,6),$ so we can substitute $x=-2$ and $y=6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+6) \\ {6}^{2} & =4p(-2+6) \\ 36 & =16p \\ p & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+6) \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{9}{4})(x+6) \\ {y}^{2} & =9(x+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{9}{4}$ is positive.
